subject: Customer traffic steering instructions and post-incident summary (APAC/EU/US)
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@fintechco.com>, ops@acme.com <ops@acme.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com, lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com, aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 3 Apr 2029 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Customer traffic steering instructions and post-incident summary (APAC/EU/US)

Hi Maria / Acme ops,

We observed a provider-level disruption that started at ~08:50 UTC affecting connectivity and service mesh peering for hosts in the following regions: us-east-1 (partial), eu-west-1 (latency spikes + increased 5xx), ap-northeast-1 (timeouts). Our control plane detected elevated tokenization errors and automated fallback kicked in for multi-region customers, but we saw increased error rates for customers scoped to a single region.

Immediate actions we recommend for applications that need continuity now:
- If you use our region-specific endpoints, switch to the global endpoint: https://api.redwood.inference/global for automatic traffic steering.
- If you manage egress IP allowlists, add the following temporary IP ranges: 34.198.0.0/16, 52.84.0.0/16 (these are our edge proxies for fallback pools).
- For customers with strict region pinning: update your config to enable cross-region fallback (example: fallback: enabled, fallback_pools: [global, eu-fallback])

We attached a short one-page "traffic steering" PDF with CLI examples and the support ticket (support_ticket_2345.txt) with the raw error metrics we collected. Our SREs are on the incident and Rishi will follow up with region-specific micro-actions.

Planned next steps from Redwood:
1) Continue rolling traffic away from the impacted subnets and into fallback pools (ongoing).
2) Share a short technical playbook per region within 1 hour.
3) Schedule a 30-minute customer briefing at 16:00 UTC to walk through the timeline and permanent mitigations.

Please confirm receipt and whether you want Redwood to perform the fallback change on your behalf (we can do a safe config flip). If you can share any blocked endpoints or if you have a phased cutover window, include that in your reply.

—
Dylan Brooks
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 415 555 0123

2) We have strict egress allowlists; please confirm the IP CIDRs are temporary and intended only while fallback is active.
3) Can you provide the exact CLI command to flip our tenant to the global endpoint? We want to test in a staging pool before doing prod.

If you can make the change for us now (staging only), that would speed things up. We'll be on the call at 16:00 UTC.

Thanks,

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@fintechco.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>, ops@acme.com <ops@acme.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com, aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 3 Apr 2029 10:05:10 +0000
Subject: Re: Customer traffic steering instructions and post-incident summary (APAC/EU/US)

Hi Maria — quick technical note and concrete steps. Short answers first: some in-flight requests were retried by our runtime (so they were delayed rather than permanently lost in most cases), but there were a small number of client-observed 5xx/errors during failover windows. The CIDRs above are temporary and managed by us; we will remove them once regional health is restored.

Region-specific recommended actions (minimal disruption):
- US (us-east-1 partial): enable the shared fallback pool and set a 1s client-side timeout for immediate relief. CLI: redwoodctl tenant update --tenant-id=fintechco --set endpoint=global --staging-only
- EU (eu-west-1): switch to quantized model variant (reduces CPU on edge) and allow cross-region KV cache warming. CLI: redwoodctl routing set --tenant fintechco --region eu --fallback-pools global,eu-fallback
- APAC (ap-northeast-1): route through asia-edge proxy for lower packet loss. CLI: redwoodctl routing set --tenant fintechco --region ap --proxy asia-edge

If you want Redwood to execute these steps for you (recommended for faster resolution) provide an explicit go-ahead and indicate which environments (staging/prod). Attached: cli-commands.txt with copy/paste-ready commands and flags.

Operational notes:
- Expected latency delta when on fallback: +20–60ms depending on model size.
- Tokenization errors we observed were due to a partial KV cache corruption during the network flapping; engineering is doing a controlled cache re-warm as we speak.
- We are tracking this under OPS-789 and HubSpot ticket FINTECH-2345.

Rishi
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Quick operational summary and next steps (for records):

What we did (by 12:30 UTC):
- Redirected affected customers to the global endpoint with your approval for staging (FinTechCo staging) — verify staging traffic looks normal.
- Enabled cross-region fallback pools for EU and APAC customers to reduce error windows.
- Opened OPS-789 and attached the raw metrics export (support_ticket_2345.txt).

Outstanding items we are tracking:
- Full RCA and timeline (will be posted to the Drive link in the next 48 hours).
- Permanent mitigations: region-aware health probes, improved early-warning metrics for KV cache degradation, and a low-latency cross-region replication path.
- Customer-facing post-incident review: scheduled 2029-04-03 16:00 UTC (30 min). Join link: https://meet.redwoodinference/incident-fintechco-0403

Action for FinTechCo: please confirm if you want Redwood to promote the same change to production after your staging validation. If we do not hear back by 15:30 UTC we will wait for your explicit sign-off.

Thanks again for your patience. We will follow up with the formal post-incident report and timeline within 48 hours.

—
Dylan Brooks
